chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Hasan ibn Dharif, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: The fathers are three: Adam, who was born a believer; the Jinn, who were born believers and disbelievers; and Iblis, who was born a disbeliever. And there is no live-bearing among them, but rather they lay eggs and hatch, and their offspring are males, with no females among them.
ai.seo_question: What are the three first fathers in Shia theology and how do they reproduce?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the unique ontological status of these three primordial fathers, distinguishing Adam as the first human monotheist, Iblis as the first disbeliever, and the Jinn as a mixed group. The hadith emphasizes their distinct reproductive nature—laying eggs rather than live birth and producing only males—which underscores their creation from fire and their role as archetypes for human spiritual states.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-186 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (ra) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma’il, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Dharif, on the authority of Aba Abdul-Rahman, on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Ammar that Abu Abdillah (as) said,

“There are three fathers: Adam, who begot believers; the Jinn, who begot both believers and disbelievers; and Satan, who begot disbelievers. None of them reproduce in the usual way, but rather they lay eggs and hatch. His offspring are males, and there are no females among them.”
